text.insert: Start with a game ISO ripped from a disc you own. This guide covers verifying that image against the upstream decompilation project's supported version. It does not provide game images, download sources, or instructions for acquiring or ripping a disc.
Known formats of GameCube games are as follows. The upstream project's build tools determine which formats you can use.

rows: Raw GameCube disc images. Compare a full-image checksum when the reference covers a complete disc dump.
Compressed disc image format used by Dolphin. Compare decompressed disc data with a raw ISO checksum.
Wii and GameCube image archive format. Requires a reader that understands the container.
Compressed disc image format used by Dolphin. Its file checksum differs from the raw disc checksum.
Compact image format that can omit unused blocks. Confirm upstream support and verify the required disc data.

steps.text: Read the upstream build instructions for the game ID, region, and disc revision. Use this exact target when choosing the reference checksum.
Use the checksum published or referenced by the upstream project for that target. Record the algorithm and whether it covers the whole disc image or an extracted file.

For a raw ISO, compute the specified checksum. For a compressed image, use a verifier that checks the decompressed disc data when the reference describes that data. A hash of an RVZ file cannot be compared directly with an ISO hash.

Require an exact match. Record the target, image format, expected and observed checksums, reference source, and verification tool. If the value differs or no reference is available, leave verification incomplete and resolve it before setup.

Once verification succeeds, place the image in the location required by the upstream build during checkout preparation. Keep the harness game ID separate from the upstream build target ID. Each identifies a different part of the setup.
